Nicht erreicht: Beton wiederholt sich im Plattentakt (gewollt, 0,647), bei 200 km/h auf Beton greift der Begrenzer leicht (≤1 dB), vier kleine Länder verfehlen ihren Betonanteil. Offen für das Ohr: ob schwere Unfälle mit 2,5 dB leiserem tiefen Schlag noch genug Wucht haben, ob die Pegeldrift je Seite natürlich oder als Schwanken wirkt, ob Ogg q5 hörbar ist. result.verdict: AU-R fixed the measured faults, and my own recordings of AU-R head 3d2e6e1 and AU-C1 head 4209268 (same scripts on both) back that up. The exact loop repetition is gone (asphalt 130: 0.635 → 0.098; cobbles 50: 0.985 → 0.183). Hash shares are now right (cobble share within 0.6 ± 0.05 in 47/47 old towns, was 0/47; concrete within ±0.05 in 14/17 countries, was 5/17). The two slab loops stay in step (offset in the audio 45 ms → ≤ 4 ms). Bridge joints are set per deck (Köhlbrand 12 → 4, stone arch 6 → 0), the fuel-lane rumble is gone (8 → 0 frames) and the wind no longer drops in tunnels. All true-peak targets hold at master volume 1.0 (heavy crash −0.66 → −1.75 dBTP, worst case −0.25 → −1.43). The impact variants keep the old timbre (≤ 0.63 dB per third-octave) and the glass/squeal/snow rules work as asked. Engine and music files are byte-identical, the 26 Ogg loops play sample-exact in the game, and every gate is green (audio_qc, run_tests 652/0, golden 20 von 20, arcade_lean). What is not fine (measured): the new 32-slab layer is +1.8 dB at 400 Hz (+1.7 at 500, +1.2 at 630), outside the ±1 dB limit. Concrete still misses R1 (0.642) because of the deliberate slab rhythm (0.26 without slabs) – a contract conflict with 'slabs.db stays 3'. The slab sync locks the AudioServer every frame on concrete, which doubles road script time (p95 0.24 → 0.60 ms, single frames 8–17 ms). The crash limiter sits exactly at its 3-dB limit (2.97/3.00 dB), and cruising at 200 km/h on concrete is borderline (0.44 dB; AU-R measured 0.96). The −1 dB on the truck boom is not justified by my data (2.66 dB with the old level), and a few cobble hits stand out by 1.6–3 dB and come back every 5.7/7 s. Nobody here can hear: whether the fuller slab knock or the standout cobbles are audible is inferred and uncertain, and the user must judge that by ear. Full German report with before/after tables: deliver/KRITIK-R/bericht.md.

result.summary: AU-R2 fixed KRITIK-R's findings on AU-R's sound rework. It kept AU-C1's character and re-measured every finding with the reviewer's own scripts, recapturing AU-C1 as "before" (all numbers measured). H1: the cause was not missing matching but the in-step crossfade (R3). Both slab designs strike at the same instants, so their strikes add partly coherently. The 32-slab patterns are now built from AU-C1's own 8 joints, in one shuffled order shared by both designs. Slab layer: +1.75 → +0.55 dB per third octave; concrete road: +1.09 → +0.32 dB. M5: the right cobble loop had two moments where all four wheels struck at once. A new seed plus matching at its playing pitch brings the loudest stone from +3.0 to +0.21 dB versus AU-C1; cobble spectra are within 0.56 dB. M1: the AudioServer is locked only when a slab loop starts and every 0.5 s (new unit test). M3: above 150 km/h the slab level rises 4 instead of 20 dB/decade (−2 dB at 200 km/h); the limiter takes 0.44/0.43/0.08/0.08 dB in four 57-s runs. M2/M4: 60 crashes each give p95 2.14 dB (car) and 2.42 dB (truck at −11); the truck at −10 gives p95 3.02 dB, so −11 stays and no level changes. H2 remains a contract question: concrete scores 0.687 with slabs at 3 dB, 0.369 at −3 dB and 0.196 without slabs. Music, engine and all other sound files are unchanged. Both drive previews in deliver/AU-R were re-recorded and the AU-R report is marked [AU-R2]. Gates are green: audio_qc with determinism, run_tests 653/0, golden 20 von 20, no frozen file changed.

contract_issues: V1/H2: R1 (< 0.40 at 0.3–3 s) measures the intended 5-m slab rhythm on concrete, not loop repetition. Measured: 0.687 with slabs.db 3 (fixed for this round), 0.196 without the slab layer, 0.369 with slabs.db −3. The lead must decide: judge R1 without slabs, or lower the slabs next round.

V3: the limits '≤ 3 dB on heavy crashes' and '≤ 0.5 dB cruising' are maxima of random variables. Measured: crash maximum 4.05 dB in 1 of 60 while p95 is 2.14 dB; cruising runs 0.08–0.44 dB. Proposal: p95 over 60 crashes, and the maximum per 60-s run over at least 4 runs.

Godot's AudioEffectHardLimiter leaves 0.05–0.14 dB of gain reduction after it has limited once, until the end of the run (measured). It is inaudible, but pre/post limiter measurements must not count it as interventions.
notes_for_next: slabs.db 3 → −3 next round: R1 on concrete then holds (0.369, measured) and M3 gets more margin (2 of 4 runs at 0.43–0.44 dB today).
Each side still repeats exactly at its own loop length; cobbles road-only reach 0.485 at 5.7 s (outside the target window). Random-offset reads for event textures would remove it.
Matching at the playing pitch (match_loop pitch) could also be applied to the other right-side loops; only the cobbles needed it this round.
On concrete, road GDScript is still +0.07–0.14 ms per frame over AU-C1, from AU-R's per-side loops and drift (inferred); optimisation is possible.

result.quality_verdict: Measured: the concrete slab layer is back to AU-C1's timbre (≤ 0.55 dB per third octave instead of 1.75). The recurring loud cobble stones are gone (+0.2 dB instead of +3 dB over AU-C1), and the slab loops no longer block the mixer every frame. Cruising at 200 km/h on concrete stays at or below 0.44 dB of limiting in four runs, and crash levels and sounds are unchanged (p95 limiting 2.1 and 2.4 dB). Music, engine and all other files are unchanged. What a player hears, inferred: at 110–150 km/h the slabs' "ta-tock" sounds as in the version the user approved, made of the very same joint strikes, just no longer repeating every 40 m. At 170 km/h the slabs are about 0.9 dB quieter and at 200 km/h about 2 dB quieter than before. Hamburg's cobbles no longer show a single loud "clack" every 7 s. Not achieved: concrete still scores 0.687 on the R1 repetition measure, because that is the slab rhythm itself (contract question). One heavy crash in 60 drove the limiter to 4 dB. Two of four 200-km/h runs sit just under the 0.5-dB limit. Nobody listened here; the user must judge the two re-recorded drive previews.
